description: Prepared concrete provider prompts; the immutable message is metadata, not literal title/overlay wording.

cases.visual_message: Akbar's administration standardized land measurement so revenue assessments could use comparable units across regions.
cases.prompt:
Setting: Late sixteenth-century Mughal agricultural administration in northern India.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, warm natural lighting, earth tones with restrained gold accents.
Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A single elegant brass measuring rod representing the Ilahi gaz lies straight across cultivated ground, right of centre. A faint golden grid overlays the land beneath it, suggesting standardized measurement. The composition is orderly, with subdued earth on the left.

cases.visual_message: The rugged Deccan landscape and its fortified strongholds formed the setting of prolonged Mughal-Maratha warfare.
cases.prompt:
Setting: The Deccan plateau in India during the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, serious reflective mood, natural lighting and muted earth tones.
Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A full-frame landscape of rugged rocky Deccan terrain with scattered hilltop fortresses. The main fortress stands on the right, with jagged rocks and sparse vegetation filling the frame. Harsh midday sunlight creates high contrast and a difficult, contested atmosphere.

cases.visual_message: Mughal revenue assessment brought land area, crop yields and prices together using averages, making taxation more systematic.
cases.prompt:
Setting: Late sixteenth-century Mughal land-revenue administration in northern India.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, warm natural lighting, earth tones with restrained gold accents.
Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A stylized visualization of columns of wheat representing yield, coins representing price, and land plots representing area merging into a single balanced golden scale on the right. The background is dark and the left side is subdued.

cases.visual_message: Maratha forces used mobile hit-and-run tactics suited to difficult terrain, frustrating conventional Mughal warfare.
cases.prompt:
Setting: The Deccan in India during late seventeenth-century Mughal-Maratha conflict.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, serious reflective mood, natural lighting and muted earth tones.
Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: Small groups of Maratha cavalry move swiftly through dense forest and rocky passes. Horses and riders blend into foliage and shadows. Dynamic motion suggests speed and stealth, contrasting with the static appearance of conventional armies.

cases.visual_message: Systematic Mughal revenue assessments made collection more predictable than ad hoc lump-sum negotiations.
cases.prompt:
Setting: Late sixteenth-century Mughal revenue administration in northern India.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, warm natural lighting, earth tones with restrained gold accents.
Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A split illustrative scene. On the left, overlapping hands exchange goods in a blurred, dark and disorderly arrangement. On the right, a neatly arranged stack of period coins and a document are sharply lit.

cases.visual_message: Tax burdens under Aurangzeb created friction and discontent among merchants.
cases.prompt:

Scene: A bustling Mughal marketplace where merchants interact with Mughal tax collectors. Their interaction occupies the centre-right, with tension and unease visible among the surrounding people. Period goods and architecture establish the market setting.

cases.visual_message: Eroding Mughal central authority left a power vacuum that other forces could exploit.
cases.prompt:
Setting: An early eighteenth-century Mughal imperial interior in India.

Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A dark, empty Mughal throne room with a single beam of light illuminating dust. The atmosphere is quiet and ominous, evoking the absence of effective central authority.

cases.visual_message: The 1765 Diwani grant gave the East India Company revenue-collection authority in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, extending its role beyond trade.
cases.prompt:
Setting: An eighteenth-century East India Company administrative setting in eastern India.
Visual treatment: Historical editorial illustration with period textures and a restrained, serious tone.
Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A stylized editorial illustration of a seal or document granting taxation rights, with faint outlines representing Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in the background. The principal document is right of centre in a serious historical composition.

cases.visual_message: Before Akbar consolidated administration, early Mughal conquests had not yet become a stable, integrated state.
cases.prompt:
Setting: Early Mughal northern India around the beginning of Akbar's reign in the sixteenth century.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, warm natural lighting, earth tones with restrained gold accents.

Scene: A stylized aged-parchment map of northern India, right of centre. Scattered disconnected red markers suggest early conquests on a dark textured background. The left side is darker and sparsely detailed.

cases.visual_message: Sambhaji's execution, intended to suppress rebellion, instead strengthened Maratha resistance.

cases.visual_message: The East India Company's acquisition of taxation rights changed its role from a trading organization toward territorial revenue administration.

cases.visual_message: Akbar divided executive responsibilities among four ministries to limit concentration of power in a single minister.

Scene: An abstract architectural illustration of four distinct ornate red-sandstone pillars supporting a central dome on the right. Subtle gold, blue, green and red accents distinguish the pillars. The background is dark with subdued space on the left.

cases.visual_message: Prolonged Deccan warfare depleted resources and devastated livelihoods, contributing to imperial financial weakness.
cases.prompt:
Setting: Peninsular India during the late seventeenth and early eighteenth-century Deccan wars.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, serious reflective mood, natural lighting and muted earth tones.
Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A desolate landscape with cracked ground, withered crops and empty granaries in peninsular India. A barren horizon emphasizes the loss of surplus grain and prosperity after prolonged conflict.

cases.visual_message: East India Company revenue collection continued during famine despite severe hardship among the population.

Setting: An eastern Indian village during the Bengal famine around 1770.

Scene: Tax collectors visit a period eastern Indian village while distressed villagers look on. Formal collection activity contrasts with the villagers' depleted surroundings and visible hardship. The principal interaction is right of centre.

cases.visual_message: Mughal governance drew on Islamic jurisprudence, local customs and imperial administrative rules rather than a single uniform legal source.
cases.prompt:
Setting: An illustrative view of law and administration in late sixteenth-century Mughal India.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, warm natural lighting, earth tones with restrained gold accents.
Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A balanced scale stands right of centre. One side holds a book representing Islamic jurisprudence, while the other holds a scroll representing local customs and an imperial decree. The surrounding surface is plain and subdued.

cases.visual_message: Weakening Mughal central control allowed regional powers to gain autonomy and fragmented imperial authority.

Setting: Early eighteenth-century India after Aurangzeb's death, with rising regional powers including the Marathas and Rajputs.

Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A stylized abstract illustration of the subcontinent's political landscape, with shrinking Mughal influence and growing Maratha and Rajput influence. Symbolic colors and shapes convey fragmentation rather than precise territorial lines.

cases.visual_message: Mir Jafar's cavalry withheld participation at Plassey, helping cause the Nawab's army to collapse into a rout.

Setting: Bengal in 1757 during the Battle of Plassey.

Scene: A wide view of a cavalry division standing inactive on a battlefield ridge, while other troops flee in disarray in the background. The contrast between stillness and disorder suggests withheld participation. The principal cavalry group is right of centre.

cases.visual_message: Severe distress in the Bengal famine continued beyond its peak years rather than ending immediately with the initial crisis.

Setting: Eastern India in the early 1770s after the main Bengal famine crisis.

Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A desolate eastern Indian landscape with a dried riverbed and sparse vegetation. Soft melancholic lighting conveys lingering environmental stress and hardship. The principal landscape feature lies right of centre.

cases.visual_message: Division of authority between Humayun and Kamran after Babur's death created rival power centres within the inherited Mughal empire.
cases.prompt:
Setting: Mughal South Asia and its Central Asian frontier after Babur's death in 1530.
Visual treatment: Cinematic historical illustration, serious reflective mood, natural lighting and muted earth tones.
Composition: Group essential content in the right half, with subdued natural surroundings on the left and upper right.
Scene: A stylized symbolic representation of divided territory, with two distinct spheres of influence pulling apart. The main arrangement is right of centre, reflecting rivalry within a fraternal division of authority.

cases.visual_message: The mansabdari system organized Mughal officers into graded ranks linking status and pay with military obligations.
cases.prompt:
Setting: Late sixteenth-century Mughal imperial administration in India.

Composition: Natural full-frame composition. Essential objects remain clearly visible above the lower quarter; upper-right background is subdued.
Scene: A vertical tiered arrangement of distinct Mughal officer silhouettes on the right. Subtle glowing numerical indicators suggest hierarchy beside the figures, which form a pyramid structure. The left side is dark and subdued.
